miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-01.question: In Micah 4:2, many nations tell one another that they should go up to the mountain of the Lord.
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-01.feedbackCorrect: The invitation comes from the nations themselves.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the invitation quoted in Micah 4:2.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-01.hint: Read what the nations say to one another.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-02.question: In Micah 4:2, tap the place the nations want to go up to.
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-02.learningObjective: Identify the mountain of the Lord as the destination.
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-02.feedbackCorrect: This is the place the invitation points to.

feedbackWrong.a: "Suas veredas" (his paths) are where to walk after learning.
feedbackWrong.c: The house of the "Deus de Jacó" comes next; the first destination named comes before.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-02.hint: Look for the first destination named in the invitation.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-03.question: According to Micah 4:1, what will the peoples do in relation to the mountain?
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-03.learningObjective: Observe the movement of the peoples.
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-03.feedbackCorrect: The text shows a crowd streaming to the exalted mountain.

feedbackWrong.a: The peoples do not flee; they head to the mountain.
feedbackWrong.b: Nothing is destroyed in this verse; the mountain is exalted.
feedbackWrong.c: The movement is of whole peoples, not only of kings.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.a: They will flee from it in fear
options.b: They will tear down its walls
options.c: They will send only their kings
options.d: They will stream to it in crowds

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-04.question: Put Micah 4:2 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-04.feedbackCorrect: The order opens with the nations, moves through the invitation and reaches God's house.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the many nations who speak: "E muitas nações".

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-04.hint: The verse begins with many nations.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-05.question: In Micah 4:2, what do the nations want God to teach them?
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-05.learningObjective: Remember what the nations ask to learn.
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-05.feedbackCorrect: Learning this changes the way the peoples live.

feedbackWrong.a: "Guerras" (wars) are what will be left behind, not taught as a way.
feedbackWrong.b: "Colheitas" (harvests) are not what they ask to be taught.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-05.hint: Think of what you learn so you can then walk in it.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-06.question: What does Micah 4:2 say that connects to this context?
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-06.learningObjective: Connect the nations' going up to their desire to learn.
miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-06.feedbackCorrect: The peoples go up because they want God to teach them.

feedbackWrong.a: They do not go up to wage war on the mountain.
feedbackWrong.b: They ask God to teach them; they do not teach him.

miqueias-sem-mq-03-monte-06.hint: See the reason for going up in the verse.

options.a: Peoples go up to wage war
options.b: Nations go up to teach God
options.c: Nations seek to learn from God

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-01.question: In Micah 4:2, the nations go up the mountain to teach God their own ways.
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-01.learningObjective: Understand who teaches and who learns.
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-01.feedbackCorrect: It is the other way around: they go up to be taught.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread who teaches and who learns in Micah 4:2.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-01.hint: See who teaches and who learns on the mountain.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-02.question: In Micah 4:2, tap the words that show why the nations go up.
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-02.feedbackCorrect: These words tie the going up to the teaching they long for.

feedbackWrong.a: "Venham" (come) is the invitation, not the reason for going up.
feedbackWrong.b: "Porque" (for) explains where the law comes from, not the first reason.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-02.hint: Look for the phrase that comes before "nos ensine" (teach us).

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-03.question: How does Micah 4:3 continue the scene of Micah 4:2?
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-03.learningObjective: Relate the nations' teaching to the end of war.
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-03.feedbackCorrect: After the teaching, God judges and the climate of war changes.

feedbackWrong.b: Training for war is abandoned, not sharpened.
feedbackWrong.c: The instruction reaches many peoples; it is not restricted.
feedbackWrong.d: The weapons become tools; they are not stored up to attack.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-03.hint: See what God does right after the nations go up.

options.a: The teaching leads to the end of war
options.b: The nations train harder for battle
options.c: Only one nation receives the instruction
options.d: The weapons are stored up to attack

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-04.question: How does the scene unfold in Micah 4:1–2?
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-04.feedbackCorrect: First the exalted mountain, then the peoples, then the request to be taught.

feedbackWrong.default: The request to learn closes the movement.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-04.hint: The teaching they ask for is the end point.

options.a: The mountain of the house is exalted
options.b: The peoples stream to the mountain
options.c: The nations ask to learn

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-05.question: In Micah 4:2, what will go out from Zion to the nations?
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-05.learningObjective: Remember what goes out from Zion.
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-05.feedbackCorrect: This is the word that guides the peoples who go up.

feedbackWrong.b: "Colheita" (harvest) is not what goes out from Zion in the verse.
feedbackWrong.c: "Guerra" (war) is what is left behind in this scene.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-05.hint: Look at the explanation at the end of the verse.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-06.question: What links Micah 4:2 to Isaiah 2:3?
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-06.learningObjective: Relate Micah and Isaiah on the nations.
miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-06.feedbackCorrect: Both prophets see peoples going up to be taught.

feedbackWrong.a: The going up seeks instruction, not battle.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text keeps the mountain for Israel alone.

miqueias-cam-mq-03-monte-06.hint: Compare who goes up, and why, in both texts.

options.a: Peoples go up to do battle
options.b: Nations go up to learn
options.c: Mountain closed to all but Israel

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-01.question: Micah 4:3 links God's instruction to the nations no longer learning war.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-01.learningObjective: Interpret the end of war in Micah 4:3.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-01.feedbackCorrect: The text joins God's judgment, transformed weapons and war forgotten.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Micah 4:3 about learning war.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-01.hint: Compare what the Lord does with what the nations stop doing.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-02.question: In Micah 4:3, tap what the swords will be turned into.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-02.learningObjective: Support the image of peace with the text.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-02.feedbackCorrect: The image trades a tool of death for work in the field.

feedbackWrong.a: "Suas espadas" (their swords) are the starting point, not the result.
feedbackWrong.c: "Nações poderosas" describes the nations corrected, not the metal's new use.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-02.hint: Look for what becomes of the metal of the weapons.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-03.question: What reading does Micah 4:3–4 support about the peace it announces?
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation of peace in Micah 4.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-03.feedbackCorrect: Peace comes from God's action and changes both weapons and daily life.

feedbackWrong.b: Rest includes ordinary people under their own plant, not only leaders.
feedbackWrong.c: Military force is exactly what leaves the scene.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not leave peace to human effort without God.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-03.hint: Put together transformed weapons and rest without fear.

options.a: God brings peace that changes life
options.b: Only rulers will have rest
options.c: Peace comes from military force
options.d: Each people makes peace without God

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Micah 4:3–4?
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-04.learningObjective: See the path from instruction to peace.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-04.feedbackCorrect: Teaching and judging lead to working and resting in peace.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the nations learning from God.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-04.hint: Think of the path from the mountain to rest.

options.a: Nations learn God's ways
options.b: Swords become tools for work
options.c: Each one rests under their own plant

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-05.question: In Micah 4:3, what will the nations no longer learn?
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-05.learningObjective: Remember what is no longer learned.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-05.feedbackCorrect: The end of training for battle marks the promised peace.

feedbackWrong.a: God's "caminhos" (ways) are learned, not abandoned.
feedbackWrong.c: "Trabalho" (work) in the field is the new use of the tools.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-05.hint: Look at the last statement of the verse.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-06.question: What links Micah 4:2 to Revelation 21:24?
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-06.learningObjective: Connect Micah's nations to the Bible's ending.
miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-06.feedbackCorrect: Micah and the end of the Bible both show peoples reached by God.

feedbackWrong.a: In the end, the nations are not left outside God's light.
feedbackWrong.b: God's presence is not a scene empty of peoples.

miqueias-pro-mq-03-monte-06.hint: Compare the place of the peoples in both passages.

options.a: Peoples stay outside the final light
options.b: The final city has no nations
options.c: Nations walk in God's light

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-01.question: In Micah 5:2, Bethlehem is called great among the thousands of Judah.
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-01.learningObjective: Notice that the promise chooses a small town.
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-01.feedbackCorrect: Bethlehem is too small to be counted. Even so, the King comes from her.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread how the prophet describes Bethlehem's size.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-01.hint: Look at the word the prophet uses for Bethlehem.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-02.question: In Micah 5:2, tap when the origins of the one coming from Bethlehem began.
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-02.learningObjective: Identify that the promised King comes from eternity.
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-02.feedbackCorrect: He is born in Bethlehem, but his origins are from before time.

feedbackWrong.b: "Milhares de Judá" (thousands of Judah) is what Bethlehem is compared with.
feedbackWrong.c: "Reinar em Israel" (rule in Israel) is what he will do, not when he comes from.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-02.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-03.question: According to Micah 5:5, who will be raised up when Assyria comes into the land?
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-03.learningObjective: Observe the response to Assyria's coming.
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-03.feedbackCorrect: The text names two groups raised up against the invasion.

feedbackWrong.a: Blacksmiths are not mentioned in the response to Assyria.
feedbackWrong.b: Priests do not appear in this verse as a defense.
feedbackWrong.c: Messengers are not raised up against Assyria here.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.a: Blacksmiths and builders
options.b: Priests of the temple
options.c: Messengers from other lands

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-04.question: Put Micah 5:4 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-04.feedbackCorrect: The order shows him standing firm, caring with God's support, and a secure people.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the ruler standing firm: "Ele se manterá firme".

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-04.hint: The verse begins with him standing firm.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-05.question: In Micah 5:4, how will the people live under the ruler's care?
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-05.feedbackCorrect: The promise includes living without fear of siege.

feedbackWrong.a: "Escondidos" (hidden) suggests fear; the text speaks of security.
feedbackWrong.c: "Sozinhos" (alone) does not describe the result of his care.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-05.hint: Look at the result that follows the ruler's care.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-06.question: What does Micah 5:2 say that connects to this context?
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-06.learningObjective: Link the promise of Bethlehem to the birth of Jesus.
miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-06.feedbackCorrect: The small town of the promise is where Joseph and Mary arrive for the birth.

feedbackWrong.b: Luke takes Joseph to the city of David, Bethlehem, not to the capital.
feedbackWrong.c: Luke names Bethlehem on purpose: the city of David.

miqueias-sem-mq-04-belem-06.hint: See which town Joseph and Mary go up to.

options.a: Jesus is born in the promised Bethlehem
options.b: Joseph takes Mary to the capital
options.c: The Gospel forgets Bethlehem

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-01.question: In Micah 5:3, after the announced birth, the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-01.learningObjective: Understand the sequence of waiting and return.
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-01.feedbackCorrect: The return is tied to the time of the birth.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the second half of Micah 5:3.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-01.hint: Read what happens to the rest of the brothers.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-02.question: In Micah 5:3, tap the word that marks the next step after the waiting.
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-02.feedbackCorrect: This word links the birth to the return of the remnant.

feedbackWrong.b: "Por isso" opens the verse explaining the handing over, not the next step.
feedbackWrong.c: "Até" (until) marks a time limit, not the turn toward the return.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-02.hint: Look for the short word after the semicolon.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-03.question: According to Micah 5:4, why will the people live securely?
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-03.learningObjective: Relate the ruler's care and security.
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-03.feedbackCorrect: Security is tied to the reach given to the ruler.

feedbackWrong.a: Little Bethlehem is not presented as a protective wall.
feedbackWrong.c: The strength mentioned upholds the ruler; it is not the people's own strength.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not say the enemies vanish through the people's effort.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-03.hint: Look for the explanation after the word "seguros".

options.a: Bethlehem had huge walls
options.b: He will be made great far and wide
options.c: Each family defended itself
options.d: The people beat their enemies alone

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-04.question: How does the promise unfold in Micah 5:3–4?
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-04.feedbackCorrect: Waiting, return and secure care form the path.

feedbackWrong.default: The ruler's secure care closes the passage.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-04.hint: The end shows the people living securely.

options.a: The people wait for the time of the birth
options.b: The rest of the brothers return to Israel
options.c: The ruler cares and brings security

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-05.question: In Micah 5:3, what will the rest of the brothers do after the birth?
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-05.learningObjective: Remember the return of the remnant.
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-05.feedbackCorrect: The return gathers the brothers back to the people.

feedbackWrong.a: "Partirá" (will leave) repeats the scattering, not the announced return.
feedbackWrong.b: "Ficará" (will stay) is not the movement at the end of the verse.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-05.hint: Look at the verb right after the word "então".

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-06.question: What links Micah 5:2 to Matthew 2:5–6?
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-06.learningObjective: Relate the Bethlehem promise and the Gospel.
miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-06.feedbackCorrect: The Gospel quotes the promise when they ask where the Christ would be born.

feedbackWrong.a: Herod's question is answered by the ancient Scripture.
feedbackWrong.c: Matthew keeps the place the scribes quoted.

miqueias-cam-mq-04-belem-06.hint: See the answer of those who knew the Scriptures.

options.a: Scripture does not answer Herod
options.b: Scribes quote the promised Bethlehem
options.c: Matthew points to another city

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-01.question: According to Micah 5:5, the promised peace depends only on armies raised against Assyria.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-01.learningObjective: Evaluate where Micah places the people's peace.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-01.feedbackCorrect: Before the shepherds, the text points to the promised one as the peace.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the first sentence of Micah 5:5.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-01.hint: See who the verse says will be the peace.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-02.question: In Micah 5:5, tap what the promised one will be for the people.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-02.learningObjective: Support the link between the promised one and peace.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-02.feedbackCorrect: Peace is tied to the promised person, not just to a tactic.

feedbackWrong.a: "Sete pastores" are raised up later; they do not sum up the first statement.
feedbackWrong.b: "Oito príncipes" appear in the defense, but the opening points elsewhere.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-02.hint: Look at the first statement of the verse.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-03.question: What reading does Micah 5:4 support about the ruler's reach?
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading of the ruler's reach.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-03.feedbackCorrect: The one born small receives a reach that goes far beyond Bethlehem.

feedbackWrong.a: The text extends his reach to the ends of the earth; it does not limit it.
feedbackWrong.b: His greatness is tied to the Lord's name, not to publicity.
feedbackWrong.d: The people's security comes from him, not in spite of him.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-03.hint: Compare the small place with the end of the verse.

options.a: He stays limited to Bethlehem
options.b: His fame depends on publicity
options.c: His reach extends to the ends of the earth
options.d: The people are secure without him

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Micah 5:2–4?
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-04.learningObjective: See the logic of the ruler's promise.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-04.feedbackCorrect: The path joins humble origin, God's strength and wide reach.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the promise tied to Bethlehem.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-04.hint: Follow from the small birthplace to the wide reach.

options.a: Little Bethlehem receives the ruler's promise
options.b: The ruler cares for the people with God's support
options.c: His reach extends to the ends of the earth

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-05.question: In Micah 5:4, in the greatness of what will the ruler care for the people, along with the Lord's name?
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-05.learningObjective: Remember the term tied to the Lord's name.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-05.feedbackCorrect: His care happens under the greatness of God's name.

feedbackWrong.b: "Presença" (presence) is a nearby truth, but it is not the missing word.
feedbackWrong.c: "Bondade" (goodness) is not the noun used in this part.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-05.hint: Look for the noun after the second "na".

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-06.question: What links Micah 5:2 to John 7:42?
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-06.learningObjective: Connect the promised Bethlehem to the hope about the Christ.
miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-06.feedbackCorrect: The hope about the Christ runs through David's village.

feedbackWrong.b: John shows people debating, without erasing the Scripture quoted.
feedbackWrong.c: The small origin stays tied to the promise.

miqueias-pro-mq-04-belem-06.hint: Compare the expected place in both passages.

options.a: The Christ comes from David's Bethlehem
options.b: The Christ would come with no tie to David
options.c: Bethlehem vanishes from the people's hopes

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.question: In Micah 7:19, God will cast all the people's sins into the depths of the sea.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.learningObjective: Observe where forgiven sins end up.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.feedbackCorrect: The final image is of sins cast far down into the deep.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread where the sins end up in Micah 7:19.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.hint: See where God casts the sins.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-02.question: In Micah 7:18, tap what God pardons in the remnant of his inheritance.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-02.feedbackCorrect: This is what the incomparable God pardons first.

feedbackWrong.a: "Transgressão" is also forgotten, but it comes later in this verse.
feedbackWrong.c: "Herança" (inheritance) is God's people, not what he pardons.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-02.hint: Look right after the opening question.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.question: According to Micah 7:18, why does God not hold on to his anger forever?
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.learningObjective: Observe the reason for God's forgiveness.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.feedbackCorrect: The reason given is God's delight in being merciful.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not say he forgot the people.
feedbackWrong.b: Fear of the people is not the reason given.
feedbackWrong.d: Weariness does not appear; the reason is joy in forgiving.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.hint: Read the explanation at the end of the verse.

options.a: He forgot about the people
options.b: He fears how the people will react
options.c: He delights in showing mercy

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-04.question: Put Micah 7:19 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-04.feedbackCorrect: Compassion, victory over wrongdoing and casting into the sea form the order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with God's compassion.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-04.hint: The verse begins with God showing compassion.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-05.question: In Micah 7:19, what will God have on us before casting the sins into the sea?
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-05.feedbackCorrect: God's tenderness opens the verse of forgiveness.

feedbackWrong.a: "Distância" (distance) is the opposite of merciful nearness.
feedbackWrong.b: "Orgulho" (pride) does not fit God's gesture here.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-05.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.question: What does Micah 7:19 say that connects to this context?
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.learningObjective: Connect forgiveness to the casting away of sins.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.feedbackCorrect: Here, forgiving means removing sin far away.

feedbackWrong.a: The sea is where the sins go, not a hiding place for the people.
feedbackWrong.b: The image does not store sins up to be charged later.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.hint: See where the sins go in the verse.

options.a: People hidden at the bottom of the sea
options.b: Sins stored up to be charged later
options.c: Forgiveness that casts sins far away

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-01.question: In Micah 7:18, God does not hold on to his anger forever because he delights in showing mercy.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-01.feedbackCorrect: The cause is stated plainly at the end of the verse.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the link between anger and mercy in 7:18.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-01.hint: Notice the "porque" (because) at the end of the verse.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-02.question: In Micah 7:18, tap the word that links God's passing anger to his mercy.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-02.feedbackCorrect: This word introduces the verse's explanation.

feedbackWrong.a: "Sempre" (forever) marks duration, not the cause given.
feedbackWrong.c: "Como" (like) opens a comparison, not the final explanation.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-02.hint: Look for the word before God's delight.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.question: How does Micah 7:19 continue the idea of Micah 7:18?
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.learningObjective: Relate mercy and the removal of sins.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.feedbackCorrect: The God who does not hold on to anger acts by casting sins far away.

feedbackWrong.b: Keeping sins contradicts casting them into the deep.
feedbackWrong.c: Forgiveness is not partial in where the sins finally end up.
feedbackWrong.d: Distance from God is not the movement of compassion.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.hint: See the action that comes after the compassion.

options.a: Mercy removes the sins
options.b: God keeps sins for later
options.c: Forgiveness leaves everything in place
options.d: Compassion drives God away from the people

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-04.question: How does the celebration unfold in Micah 7:18–19?
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-04.learningObjective: Understand how the celebrated forgiveness unfolds.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-04.feedbackCorrect: A question, forgiveness without lasting anger, and sins sent to the deep.

options.a: Micah announces the ruler coming from Bethlehem
options.b: The scribes point Herod to Bethlehem
options.c: The child is born and laid in a manger

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: In Micah 5:2, what word shows where the ruler's roots come from?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Remember the term for the ruler's origin.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: This word ties the ruler to a past older than Bethlehem.

feedbackWrong.a: Beginnings ("começos") is generic; the verse uses its own term.
feedbackWrong.c: Roots ("raízes") is a similar idea, but not the word in the text.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.question: What links Micah 5:2 to John 7:42?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.learningObjective: Connect the Bethlehem promise to the expectation about the Christ.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, Bethlehem is tied to the expected Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: The small village stays at the center of the expectation.
feedbackWrong.c: John records the people's question without denying the place.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-02-belem-.hint: Look at the place named in both passages.

options.a: Bethlehem plays no part in the expectation
options.b: The Christ comes from David's Bethlehem
options.c: The Christ would come only from Galilee

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 4:3, the nations will keep learning war after transforming their weapons.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Review the end of war in Micah 4.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: The text closes the scene of war; it does not continue it.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Read what happens to war at the end of the verse.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 4:3, tap what the swords will be turned into.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Review the transformation of the weapons.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: A weapon of war becomes a farming tool.

feedbackWrong.a: The swords are what get transformed; they are not the end result.
feedbackWrong.c: The spears become another tool, named later.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look for the first result of the transformation.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: According to Micah 5:2, where will the one who is to rule in Israel come from?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: The promise names the small town of Judah.

feedbackWrong.a: Egypt appears in Micah 7 as the past, not as the origin.
feedbackWrong.c: Jerusalem is named in Micah 4, not as the origin in 5:2.
feedbackWrong.d: Samaria is not the place named in this promise.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Read who is called by name in the verse.

options.a: From Egypt, the ancient land
options.b: From Bethlehem, small in Judah

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: Put Micah 7:19 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Review the order of the final forgiveness.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Compassion and casting into the depths close the book with forgiveness.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with God's compassion for his people.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: The verse begins with an act of God.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 4:4, under what plant will each one sit without fear?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: The first plant named marks safe rest.

feedbackWrong.b: The fig tree ("figueira") comes right after, in the same sentence.
feedbackWrong.c: The olive tree ("oliveira") is not the first plant in this verse.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look at the first plant named in the verse.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: What does Micah 4:2 say that connects to this context?
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Connect the scenes to the God who teaches.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: All three scenes start with God teaching his people and the nations.

feedbackWrong.a: Small Bethlehem shows that size does not rule the promise.
feedbackWrong.c: The final forgiveness does not keep sins close to the people.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look at the reason for going up the mountain.

options.a: Size decides whom God uses
options.b: God brings together teaching, king and pardon
options.c: Sins stay close so they can be charged

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 5:4, tap how far the ruler will be made great.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: His reach goes far beyond Bethlehem.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the strength behind his care, not the reach named.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the name that sustains his care, not the limit.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look for the expression of reach at the end of the verse.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: Put Micah 5:2 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Review the order of the Bethlehem promise.
miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Name, size and promise appear in this order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start by calling Bethlehem by name.

miqueias-sem-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: The verse begins by calling someone by name.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 4:2–3, learning God's ways comes before weapons become tools.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Understand the order between teaching and peace.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: First the going up to learn, then the weapons are transformed.

feedbackWrong.false: Compare the order between Micah 4:2 and 4:3.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Follow the order: does teaching come before or after the weapons?

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 4:2, tap the words that show why the nations go up.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Review the purpose of going up.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: The going up has a goal: to be taught by God.

feedbackWrong.a: "Venham" is the opening invitation, not the reason.
feedbackWrong.b: "porque" explains where the law comes from, at the end of the verse.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look for the expression tied to the verb "ensine".

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: How does Micah 5:4 describe the care of the ruler from Bethlehem?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Relate the Bethlehem origin to the ruler's care.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: He governs leaning on God, and the people live secure.

feedbackWrong.a: His own strength alone is not what the verse highlights.
feedbackWrong.c: Distance from the people contradicts the verb "cuidará" used here.
feedbackWrong.d: Fear is not the result; the text speaks of living secure.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: See whom the ruler leans on to give care.

options.a: Governs with his own strength alone
options.b: Cares for them, relying on God's strength
options.c: Stays far from the besieged people
options.d: Brings fear to those he governs

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: How does the scene move forward in Micah 4:1–2?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Understand the movement from the mountain to the nations.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Exalted mountain, peoples arriving and teaching requested form the movement.

feedbackWrong.default: The request to learn is the point of arrival.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: The requested teaching closes this movement.

options.a: The mountain of the house is exalted
options.b: The peoples stream to the exalted mountain
options.c: The nations ask for God's teaching

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 4:2, what will go out from Zion to guide the nations?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Review what goes out from Zion.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: It is the instruction that goes out to the peoples who came up.

feedbackWrong.b: War ("guerra") is abandoned, not sent out as a guide.
feedbackWrong.c: A harvest ("colheita") is not what goes out from Zion here.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look at the final explanation in the verse.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: What links Micah 4:2 to Isaiah 2:3?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Relate Micah and Isaiah on the nations.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Both texts see nations seeking instruction on the mountain.

feedbackWrong.b: The going up seeks teaching, not battle.
feedbackWrong.c: The mountain is not presented as a closed place.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Compare who goes up, and why, in the two texts.

options.a: Nations go up to learn
options.b: Peoples go up to fight
options.c: A mountain closed to all but Israel

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 7:18, tap the word that explains why the anger does not last forever.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Review the cause of the final forgiveness.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: The explanation comes right after this word.

feedbackWrong.a: "sempre" measures duration; it gives no explanation.
feedbackWrong.b: "como" opens the first question of the verse.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look for the word before God's joy.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: How does the celebration move forward in Micah 7:18–19?
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Understand the movement of forgiveness in Micah 7.
miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Pardon, anger that does not stay and sins cast away form the movement.

feedbackWrong.default: The depths of the sea close the celebration of forgiveness.

miqueias-cam-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Casting into the sea is the final point.

options.a: God pardons the remnant of his inheritance
options.b: He does not keep his anger forever
options.c: He casts the sins into the depths

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: According to Micah 5:2, Bethlehem matters because it was the biggest among the thousands of Judah.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Evaluate the reading that measures Bethlehem by size.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Its importance lies in the promise, not in the size of the town.

feedbackWrong.true: The text calls Bethlehem too small among the thousands.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: See how Micah describes the size of Bethlehem.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 7:18, tap what God delights in showing when he forgives.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Support God's character with the text.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: This trait explains why the anger does not last forever.

feedbackWrong.a: "transgressão" is the wrong forgotten, not what he gladly shows.
feedbackWrong.c: "herança" is his people, not the trait he shows.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look at the end of the verse, after the explanation.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: Which reading best brings together the promises of Micah 4, 5 and 7?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Choose the reading that unites the three scenes.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: God teaches, raises up the ruler and forgives in the end.

feedbackWrong.b: Military strength is transformed, not celebrated as the final way.
feedbackWrong.c: Sins cast into the depths are not kept to be charged.
feedbackWrong.d: The small place is chosen, not discarded by the promise.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Put together the mountain, Bethlehem and the depths of the sea.

options.a: God teaches, reigns and forgives
options.b: Strong weapons secure the future
options.c: Forgiveness keeps sins close by

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: Which sequence reveals the thread of the promises in Micah 4, 5 and 7?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: See the thread that unites the three scenes.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Teaching, ruler and pardon show God's kind rule.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the nations learning on the mountain.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Follow the order of the chapters reviewed.

options.a: Nations learn the ways of God
options.b: The ruler from Bethlehem cares for the people
options.c: God casts the sins into the sea

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 5:2, the ruler's origins go back to the days of what?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: His origin goes beyond the history of the small town.

feedbackWrong.a: History ("história") sounds vague next to the weight of the verse's end.
feedbackWrong.b: Youth ("juventude") would shrink the origin to a short stage.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look at the last words of the verse.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: What links Micah 5:2 to Matthew 2:5–6?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: Connect the Bethlehem promise to its later quotation.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Matthew records the ancient promise being quoted to those who asked.

feedbackWrong.a: The quotation shows the ancient promise was still remembered.
feedbackWrong.b: The Gospel confirms the place; it does not swap it for another.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look at the answer given about where the Christ would be born.

options.a: The ancient promise was forgotten
options.b: Matthew swaps the place of the promise
options.c: Scribes point to the promised Bethlehem

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: In Micah 5:2, tap the phrase that shows how ancient the ruler's origins are.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: This phrase points to a story older than his birth.

feedbackWrong.b: That describes the size of the place, not his time.
feedbackWrong.c: That measures Bethlehem among the towns, not his origin.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Look for the part of the verse tied to the distant past.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.question: Which sequence reveals God's faithfulness celebrated in Micah 7?
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.learningObjective: See God's faithfulness across the book.
miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.feedbackCorrect: Promise to the fathers, the exodus remembered and present pardon meet.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the promise made to the ancient fathers.

miqueias-pro-miqueias-miqueias-03-desafi.hint: Go from the ancient promise to the present pardon.

options.a: God promised mercy to the ancient fathers
options.b: He showed wonders when Israel left Egypt
options.c: Micah celebrates the God who forgives
